GitHub widened the range to <= 4.0.7 on 2026-11-17, so the newest release, 4.0.7 (published 2026-08-24), is inside it and every copy is flagged. The trigger is a glob PATTERN with repeated extglobs, compiled by picomatch and matched against a string. Two copies are installed: node_modules/picomatch 4.0.7 and node_modules/micromatch/node_modules/picomatch 2.3.2 (required by micromatch 4.0.8 as ^2.3.1, reached through eslint-config-next -> @next/eslint-plugin-next -> fast-glob 3.3.1, lint tooling). So no pattern is built from user input, and in the deployed server or the browser bundle picomatch is loaded at most as an unused module in the config load and never called (next-intl's request-time code, next-intl/server and the client, does not import plugin.cjs). No app or shared code imports picomatch; only scripts/lint-config.test.mjs and scripts/vitest-force-rerun.test.mjs call it, on repo-owned patterns, in tests.
